urn:csabs:concept/HeapStore.axiomBasis: dom(h) is a finite subset of positive addresses; heap equality is lookup equality; a∈dom(h) ⇒ write(h,a,v)(b)=Some(v) if b=a, else h(b); a∈dom(h) ⇒ free(h,a)(b)=None if b=a, else h(b); (a,h′)∈alloc(h,v) ⇔ a∉dom(h) ∧ h′=h[a↦v]
urn:csabs:concept/HeapStore.basisScope: Pure mathematical snapshots. Unallocated read/write/free is undefined (None); stored values may themselves encode options. Allocation nondeterministically chooses any fresh positive address; address reuse after free allowed. No pointer arithmetic, GC, permissions, typing or concurrency assumed.
urn:csabs:concept/HeapStore.definition: A finite map from nonnull addresses to values, with partial allocated-cell access and fresh allocation.
urn:csabs:concept/HeapStore.mathematicalFormulation: A heap is a finite partial map h:ℕ_{>0}⇀V. write/free require a∈dom(h); allocation chooses a∉dom(h) and produces h[a↦v]. Invalid accesses return none and allocation is relational.
